sources_considered.why: Read the contemporary financial report. No primary ChatGPT unit-economics disclosure was found; this reputable report concerns company-wide annual estimates.
Read the survey authors' report on August 2024 usage. It measures individuals' use and includes ChatGPT.
Read the official working paper summary. Its observations end in February 2024 and measure all AI used in production, so they do not match the target period or generative-AI-specific scope.
Search surfaced API-margin estimates rather than ChatGPT prompt economics. Not used as evidence.

evidence_items.explanation: The report corroborates expected company-wide losses, not realized losses on each ChatGPT prompt. Its annual period, company-wide scope and inclusion of overhead prevent a decisive comparison with the contract.

metric_scope.metric: Expected company-wide annual loss, excluding some expenses

evidence_items.explanation: The representative survey reports substantial individual usage, including 28.1% work-related use among employed respondents. This challenges a broad claim of little adoption evidence, but does not isolate paid enterprise software or exclude ChatGPT.

unresolved_gaps: No matched ChatGPT revenue, cost and usage breakdown establishes losses on every prompt.
No cost-allocation rule connects annual company losses to individual prompts.
The adoption evidence does not resolve the speaker's distinction between ChatGPT use and actual generative AI software.
No adoption threshold or geographic population is specified.
